'''María del Carmen Martínez Sancho''' (8 July 1901 in Toledo – 15 October 1995 in Malaga) was the first woman in Spain to gain a PhD in Mathematics. She was the first Professor of Mathematics to work in secondary school education in Spain, and the first woman to be appointed to the ''Board of Extension of Studies'' at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin|University of Berlin]]. She was part of Madrid and Seville's ''Instituto-Escuela.''<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://tribunafeminista.elplural.com/2017/07/maria-del-carmen-martinez-sancho-pionera-de-las-matematicas-espanolas/|title=María del Carmen Martínez Sancho: pionera de las matemáticas españolas |date=9 July 2017|work=Tribuna Feminista|access-date=11 July 2018|language=es-ES}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Martínez was born on 8 July 1901 in Toledo.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Hontangas|first=Natividas Aranque|year=2017|title=Carmen Martínez Sancho, una pionera de las matemáticas en España: la renovación pedagógica y su relación con la Junta de Ampliación de Estudios|url=https://dialnet.unirioja.es/servlet/articulo?codigo=5834873|journal=Pecia Complutense: Boletín de la Biblioteca Histórica "Marqués de Valdecilla"|language=es|issue=26|pages=1–16|issn=1698-272X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ceies.cchs.csic.es/?q=content/mart%C3%ADnez-sancho-mar%C3%ADa-del-carmen|title=Martínez Sancho, María del Carmen {{!}} JAE educa|website=ceies.cchs.csic.es|access-date=11 July 2018}}</ref> She was the second of six children in the family of José Martínez and Emilia Sancho.<ref name=":1" /> Her father was an engineer and public worker, which resulted in the family living in several Spanish cities before they settled in Madrid.<ref name=":1" /> Her father was keen for his children to receive their education at the ''[[Institución Libre de Enseñanza]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.matematicasdigitales.com/carmen-martinez-sancho-una-pionera-en-las-matematicas-espanolas/|title=Carmen Martínez Sancho, una pionera en las matemáticas españolas – Matemáticas Digitales|date=9 December 2015|work=Matemáticas Digitales|access-date=11 July 2018|language=es-ES}}</ref> He believed that boys and girls should have the same education, and supported her to complete high school classes at the [[University of Alcalá]]'s Cardenal Cisneros Associated School.<ref name=":1" /> Here she became interested in mathematics and literature, and her parents encouraged her toward mathematics.<ref name=":1" /> Martínez herself was unhappy with the school: all students scored highly and there were no clear criteria for success. She finished her high school studies on 1 July 1918.<ref name=":1" />

In 1918 she began to study in sciences the [[Complutense University of Madrid|Central University of Madrid]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|title=Historia de la educación en España y América.|date=1992–1994|publisher=Ediciones SM|others=Bartolomé Martínez, Bernabé., Delgado Criado, Buenaventura., Fundación Santa María (Madrid, Spain)|isbn=8471123746|location=Madrid|oclc=28022427}}</ref> In the first year of her degree, she was taught by extraordinary teachers, including [[:es:Cecilio Jiménez Rueda|Cecilio Jiménez Rueda]] and [[Julio Rey Pastor]].<ref name=":1" /> Throughout her career, her greatest influence would be [[Julio Rey Pastor]] who taught her [[Mathematical analysis|Mathematical Analysis]].<ref name=":0" /> Carmen was a prestigious student since she got the highest marks in the year. Whist still an undergraduate student she was asked to teach at the ''Instituto-Escuela'' of Madrid where her younger siblings studied. She gave classes simultaneously with her university studies. She graduated on 7 December 1926.<ref name=":1" />

She began her doctorate studies under the supervision of [[:es:José María Plans y Freyre|José María Plans y Freyre]] who was the first person to introduce relativity to Spain. Her thesis was titled: ''The concept of function, continuous and semicontinuous functions, and their properties''.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded the ''Extraordinary Price of Doctorate'' for her doctoral thesis and became the first Spanish woman to earn a PhD in mathematics.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mujeresconciencia.com/2017/07/06/maria-del-carmen-martinez-sancho-pionera-las-matematicas-espanolas-principios-del-siglo-xx/|title=María del Carmen Martínez Sancho: pionera de las matemáticas españolas de principios del siglo XX {{!}} Vidas científicas {{!}} Mujeres con ciencia|work=Mujeres con ciencia|access-date=11 July 2018|language=es-ES}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1928 Martínez was appointed Professor of Mathematics in the High-School Institute of Ferrol (La Coruña).<ref name=":1" /> She would go on to become a teacher of the ''El Instituto Femenino Infanta Beatriz'' with her colleague [[:es:Carmen Vielva Otorel|Carmen Vielva Otorel]].<ref name=":1" />

=== Germany ===
On 4 November 1930 the Board of Extension of Studies granted her an eight-month grant to move to Germany to continue her studies on Multidimensional Geometry.<ref name=":1" /> She attended classes given by [[Kurt Hensel]] at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin|University of Berlin]]. She extended her grant for two extra months, eventually finishing her work on 2 September 1932.<ref name=":1" /> She presented a memorial project that detailed Hammerstein's and Bieberbach's classes.<ref name=":1" />

=== Seville ===
Immediately after returning to Spain from Germany, Martínez began to teach at ''Instituto-Escuela.'' She describes the time in Seville as one of the highlights of her career.<ref name=":1" /> Whilst in Seville she met Alberto Meléndez, who would become her husband and father of her child, Alberto Meléndez Martínez.<ref name=":1" />

Martínez moved to the Murillo Institute.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Juan|first=Núñez Valdés|last2=Rocío|first2=Maraver Alonso|date=2009|title=Carmen Martínez Sancho y el Instituto Murillo de Sevilla : una relación de entrega y generosidad|hdl=11441/39572|isbn=9788469257159}}</ref> She taught the first, third and fifth grade in 1938 and was promoted to Professor in 1939. Martínez organised a campaign within the Institute to build a canteen to provide food for disadvantaged students.<ref name=":1" /> Her campaign suffered due to the rise of [[Francoist Spain|Francoism]].<ref name=":1" /> Her high school colleague Patricio Peñalver Bachiller, Professor and Dean in the Faculty of Sciences of the [[University of Seville]], encouraged her to apply for faculty position.<ref name=":1" /> She was appointed a Professor of Mathematics in 1957.<ref name=":1" />

=== Return to Madrid ===
Martínez retired from the Murillo Institute in 1974, returned to Madrid and taught mathematics in the Jesús María School of Vallecas.<ref name=":1" /> Again she made efforts to engage students of low socioeconomic status.<ref name=":1" />

=== Recognition ===
As an acknowledgement to her teaching labour, Seville's town hall named one of their streets of the Santa Justa district in her honour.<ref name=":0"/>
